chunks.subject: AP Psychology
chunks.title: FRQ 1 Article Analysis Question (AAQ) — 7 points — Set 1
chunks.content: AP Psychology FRQ 1 is the Article Analysis Question (AAQ), 7 points, based on a source study. Scored by parts (Part A–F). General rules: a response earns a point only if it clearly addresses the source study's topic; the concept must be APPLIED to the prompt (a definition alone does not earn the point); a response is not penalized for extra incorrect information unless it directly contradicts otherwise-correct content. Typical parts: A identify the research method used in the study (e.g., experiment); B identify the operational definition of a variable / the population; C describe the meaning of a statistical result (e.g., correlation, effect); D identify a control or explain a design feature; E–F apply psychological concepts to the study and explain how a finding supports or limits a conclusion. Common failure: defining a concept without applying it to the study; misidentifying the research method; contradictory dual definitions (which void the point).

chunks.subject: AP Psychology
chunks.title: AAQ Set 1 exemplar — Sample 1A, 7/7
chunks.content: AAQ (Set 1) scored 7/7 — correctly identified the research method, applied each concept to the study, described the statistical result accurately, and explained how the findings support the conclusion. Full-credit model for the Article Analysis Question.

chunks.subject: AP Psychology
chunks.title: AAQ Set 1 exemplar — Sample 1B, 4/7
chunks.content: AAQ (Set 1) scored 4/7 — earned the identification and simpler application parts but lost points where concepts were defined without being applied to the study, or where the result/design explanation was incomplete. Illustrates the common AAQ miss: definition without application.

chunks.subject: AP Psychology
chunks.title: AAQ Set 1 exemplar — Sample 1C, 2/7
chunks.content: AAQ (Set 1) scored 2/7 — earned only a couple of parts (e.g., research-method identification and one application), losing most application/explanation points. Illustrates a response that engages the study only superficially.
